article.title: Sheinbaum Pursues Failed Neo-liberal Policies, Says Mexican Communist Leader
article.author: MLToday
article.content: By Tim Pelzer September 21, 2026 The Guardian (Australia) MEXICO CITY – The social democratic government of Claudia Sheinbaum is continuing the same failed neo-liberal policies of the previous Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador administration, said Angel Chavez, member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of Mexico (PCM) in an interview. Instead of diversifying export markets and strengthening national production, the Sheinbaum National Regeneration Movement (MORENA) government is trying to save and extend the US, Mexico, Canada Agreement ( USMCA) for another 16 years, a free trade pact that replaced NAFTA in 2020. “The deal primarily benefits the monopolies in the three member countries and has limited the country’s independence. The agreement tells each country what they can buy and sell. In the past Mexico was self-sufficient in corn — an important component of the diet — now it must import genetically modified corn from the US”, he said in a interview. When the free trade agreement was first signed in 1994, it ruined Mexican agriculture by allowing the US to flood the market with cheap corn, wheat and other products, bankrupting many farmers and impoverishing the countryside. The USMCA has halted the country’s economic development and turned Mexico into a low-wage maquiladora , dominated by foreign companies that import raw materials or components duty free, assemble them and then re-export finished products to the US and Canada. These plants, which employ millions of Mexicans and form a major part of the country’s manufacturing sector, take advantage of low wages and a six-day work week in Mexico. In the past the Mexican left opposed free trade with the US but now MORENA supports it, he said. Chavez complained the Sheinbaum government has also caved in to US demands to keep Chinese investment out of Mexico. “The USMCA even allows North American inspectors into factories to decide if a union meeting is legal”, claimed Chavez. The PCM opposes the Sheinbaum government’s attempts to save the USMCA and wants Mexico to pull out of the agreement. “MORENA does not want to overthrow capitalism but instead promised that it wanted to reform it and make it more beautiful through reforms, but now it does not want to even do that”, complained Chavez. During the 1980s and 1990s right-wing PRI and PAN [PRI and PAN are Mexican bourgeois parties] governments privatized hundreds of companies for well below their market value. “The first MORENA government of Lopez Obrador never re-nationalized these companies. Sheinbaum continues with his program.” MORENA`s approach to mass youth unemployment is a program called “Young People Constructing the Future”, started by Lopez Obrador in 2019 when he was first elected. “The government pays the wages of 3.5 million young people each year who work for private companies, providing free labor to capitalists at taxpayers’ expense,“ lamented Chavez. Workers are paid the minimum wage of 9,500 pesos per month and employers are not obligated to continue employing them after one year. He also challenged MORENA`s claim it has raised the minimum salary by 250% since 2019. “This is only a decree and has not been enforced. In many cases the government does not even obligate employers to pay the minimum wage.” When asked if MORENA governments have reduced poverty through the introduction of new social programs, he said that high inflation has been undermining these programs. He said that monopolies have been raising prices for basic goods, making it impossible to reduce poverty levels in the country. “These social programs were introduced primarily to win votes for MORENA and buy social peace and stability”. He said the country still has 50 million poor people [Mexico’s population is an estimated 133 million] and suffers from mass unemployment, compelling 55% of the labor force to work in the informal sector such as selling goods or food on the street because there is no unemployment insurance or welfare. “These conditions have force many Mexicans to migrate to the US and Canada,” he said. He is also critical of Sheinbaum for not protecting the 10 million Mexican immigrants living in the US. Recently it was reported that 18 Mexicans have died in ICE detention centers. “The government has not protested or did anything to help migrants. Instead it is helping the US deport immigrants back to Mexico.” The MORENA party government also stopped shipping oil to Cuba, helping to worsen the US blockade, lamented Chavez. Chavez said the PCM was not able to get its electoral registration back this year because of rules designed to keep opposition parties off the ballot. Mexican electoral authorities require a new party to submit 350 thousand signatures and hold costly assemblies in all 31 states, which proved impossible for the PCM to meet. He said MORENA has not expressed any intention to change these rules. Since its refounding in 1994, the PCM has been unable to regain its former electoral registration that it was granted in 1978. The party ran candidates in 1979, winning 5.4 % of the vote and electing 18 deputies to the National Parliament, becoming the third largest party in the country. In 1981, party members dissolved the party to form the Mexican Unified Socialist Party (PMS). In 1988, the PMS dissolved and formed the Democratic Revolution Party (PRD). The PRD – to which Lopez Obrador belonged during the first part of his political career, and which he abandoned to form MORENA in 2011 – inherited the PCM`s electoral registration and property. Denied ballot access for the 2024 elections, the PCM ran Marco Vinicio Davila for president as well as several candidates for state governor as write-in candidates – including Angel Chavez in Mexico City — which is allowed by the Mexican constitution. PCM candidates received 85,000 write-in votes and probably more since the party has evidence that many votes were marked as null. Chavez characterized the party’s electoral campaign as successful, especially the presidential race, despite a media blackout by the national television networks. He said Vinicio Davila traveled the country speaking at meetings, distributing tens of thousands of leaflets with volunteers, door knocking and giving interviews to media. “Marco became well know across the country”, remarked Chavez. “While l was campaigning with Marco in Mexico City where l was the candidate for governor, l remember people constantly approaching Marco on the street to speak with him.” Until the party can get back its electoral registration, Chavez said the PCM will continue running write-in candidates to offer a socialist alternative to the working class.
